data.gender_notes: Marti is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek name Martia, which is a feminine form of Mars, the Roman god of war. In Christianity, the name Marti is associated with Saint Marta, who is believed to have been a disciple of Jesus and the sister of Mary Magdalene. Marti is a name of strong and compassionate women, like Mary, who are devoted to their faith and loved ones.

data.etymology: Marti belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mary like.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Marti total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Marti has a rich cultural heritage, blending the Roman and Christian traditions. It is a name that speaks of bravery, strength, and resilience - qualities associated with the Roman god Mars and the fiery spirit of the early Christian disciples. The name also connects us with the deep history of the faith and its roots in the ancient world.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Marti carries the powerful message of devotion and deep faith. In the story of Saint Marta, we see a woman who was fully committed to her spiritual journey, supporting her sister Mary as they devotedly followed Jesus. The name Marti is a reminder of the importance of staying true to our faith, and offering love, support, and strength to those around us. It is a name imbued with the power of prayer and the grace of God.
